summary: Sustainability is discussed, but the cost model should more explicitly cover the recurrent work hidden behind ‘shared’ …
comment: Sustainability is discussed, but the cost model should more explicitly cover the recurrent work hidden behind ‘shared’ infrastructure: metadata and terminology maintenance, hosting, connectivity/power, devices, cybersecurity, upgrades, integration regression testing, user support, supervision, data-quality work, community engagement and safe decommissioning. Capital funding without these functions creates brittle infrastructure.

reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo

public.text: Sustainability is discussed, but the cost model should more explicitly cover the recurrent work hidden behind ‘shared’ infrastructure: metadata and terminology maintenance, hosting, connectivity/power, devices, cybersecurity, upgrades, integration regression testing, user support, supervision, data-quality work, community engagement and safe decommissioning. Capital funding without these functions creates brittle infrastructure.
public.suggestedRevision: Require a 5–10 year total-cost-of-ownership and transition plan covering central and subnational recurrent costs, like local support ecosystems, refresh/upgrade cycles, security and incident response, training/supervision, accessibility, vendor exit, data migration and decommissioning. Link scale decisions to demonstrated financing and operational capacity.
